Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

thank God! interjection

also thank heavens, thank goodness, thank the Lord, thanks be to God

late Latin

Vulg. 1 Cor. 15.57: Deō autem grātiās, quī dedit nōbīs victōriam
Vulg. 2 Cor. 9.15: Grātiās Deō super inēnarrābilī dōnō ejus.

Deō grātiās!

thanks be to God!

The Christian form, from Paul’s letters; the household’s word.

Other words

  • Dīs grātia! — thank the gods!

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 121: Est, dīs grātia; Ter. Hec. 346c: Dīs grātiam habeō.

    (vōx cōmica: Ter.)

    The classical (pagan) phrase; dīs grātiam habeō, “I thank the gods”, in full.

  • Laus superīs! — thank heavens!

    also used · modern · Traupman 18: thank heavens, laus superīs

    (superī: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor., Ov.)

    Traupman’s phrase; Lewis & Short does not quote it. Superī, the gods above, is mostly poetic; comedy says Dīs grātia.

Examples

  • Deō autem grātiās, quī dedit nōbīs victōriam per Dominum nostrum Jēsum Chrīstum.

    But thanks be to God, who has given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.Vulg. 1 Cor. 15.57

  • Quid ais? an vēnit Pamphilus? — Vēnit. — Dīs grātiam habeō.

    What are you saying? Has Pamphilus come? — He has. — Thank God.Ter. Hec. 346–346c

  • Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.

    The gods are keeping me safe; all’s well.Plaut. Aul. 207

See also phew!, God forbid!, give thanks, thank you.
